def: Text that creates requirements a conforming implementation must meet, usually signalled by keywords such as shall, should and may defined in the document's conventions. Contrast with informative text, which only explains.
A field whose stored value is one less than the quantity it represents (e.g. NLB = 7 means 8 logical blocks; a queue size field of 1023 means 1024 entries).
A field, bit or value set aside for future definition. The document's conventions say how writers and readers treat it; a reserved field in one revision may be defined in a later one.
PCIe register attribute: software clears a status bit by writing 1 to it; writing 0 has no effect.
The NVM Express mechanism for proposing and ratifying a change or new feature; ratified TPs are integrated into later specification revisions.
A personal or team reference with one row per decoded field: location, width, encoding, owner, reader, revision and citation by document and section name.

The 16-byte structure an NVMe controller writes into a Completion Queue to report a command's completion: command-specific Dword 0, SQ head and identifier, Command Identifier, Phase Tag and Status Field.
The 64-byte NVMe command written by the host into a Submission Queue: CDW0 (opcode, CID), NSID, metadata and data pointers, and command Dwords 10–15.
A family of specifications defining a queue-based interface and command sets for non-volatile memory, mapped onto PCIe, RDMA and TCP transports.
A small PCIe packet exchanged between link partners for acknowledgements (Ack/Nak), flow control updates and power management; it never leaves the link.
The PCIe packet that carries a request or completion (memory, I/O, configuration, message) between two devices.
Bit 16 of CQE Dword 3. The controller inverts the value it writes each time it wraps the Completion Queue, letting the host recognise new entries without reading a register.
An NVMe data pointer entry naming a host memory page; PRP1/PRP2 in the SQE, plus PRP lists for larger transfers. Only the first entry may have a non-zero page offset.
The course's evidence-defined ordinal scale for claims: CONFIRMED, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, UNKNOWN. It is not a probability unless calibrated against outcome data.
An observation or experiment that would show a hypothesis is wrong if it came out a particular way; required for every hypothesis in a senior analysis.
The earliest observed departure from expected behaviour in the evidence; the starting point of root-cause reasoning, not necessarily the root cause.
A trace record converted into one common schema (stable ID, time, direction, layer, kind, decoded fields, correlation links, provenance) independent of the capture tool.
A value shared by related events that lets them be linked: (Requester ID, Tag) for request and completion, queue slot, (SQID, CID) for SQE and CQE, data address ranges, interrupt vector.
A derived event standing for an expected event that did not occur by a deadline; dated at the deadline and treated as unknown if the deadline falls outside the capture or in a gap.
The pipeline stage that applies documented, cited rules to correlated events and emits findings, each with evidence event IDs.
A capture from a known-good system and workload, used as the expected baseline when comparing or testing analysis tools.
A PCIe completion status (and error type) meaning the completer does not support or cannot route the request.
A machine-learning model that generates text; useful for explanation and drafting, unreliable as a source of packets, field values or specification requirements.
Selecting the evidence and reference passages a model is given: event windows, command records, context and cited specification text, keyed by the findings.
Backing every statement about a specification with a retrieved, cited passage (document, revision, section name), preserving its normative strength.
Output from a language model that is fluent but not supported by its inputs, such as invented packets, values or requirements.
Deterministic code that checks analysis claims: cited events exist, asserted field values match the decode, confidence rules hold, causal claims share identifiers.
Host hardware that translates and checks device DMA addresses (IOVAs); an unmapped access is typically refused, which a PCIe device sees as an unsuccessful completion.
The PCIe agent that originates a request, identified by its Requester ID (Bus/Device/Function).
The PCIe agent that services a request and, for non-posted requests, returns the completion.
A 16-bit value chosen by the host in CDW0 of an SQE, unique among outstanding commands in that SQ, returned in the CQE to match completion to command.
A Data Link Layer Packet telling the transmitter that a TLP was received in error; the transmitter replays from its replay buffer.

exp: Link Training and Status State Machine
def: The PCIe Physical Layer state machine that brings a link up, trains it, and handles recovery and power states.
Field of the NVMe Controller Capabilities register; doorbell registers are spaced (4 << DSTRD) bytes apart starting at offset 1000h.
